text:
morgan: Noticed an uptick in host CPU and grpc smallwrite tails after yesterday's kernel-chooser flip on canary pool-7. p50 host CPU +9%. Anyone tracking?

sasha: I saw that too. Ran a 5k replay and p50 went 38ms->42ms, p99 210ms->290ms. Flamegraph narrows it to token_proc::classify and utf8::scalar_fallback.

priya: Which chooser change exactly? We recently toggled the short-seq scalar path to prefer low-latency microkernel when frag_count<=2.

ash: Correct. The scalar microkernel avoids the vectorized utf8 fastpath but inserts an extra assemble memcpy when a proto frame is split. More fragments = more writes.

morgan: Perf sample from a canary host:
```
# perf top -p $PID
 token_proc::classify  22.1%
 net::writev_batch       12.0%
 http2::frame_mux        8.7%
 kv::lookup             5.4%
```

replay-bot: replay summary (pool-7 canary): 5k reqs, baseline p50=38ms p99=210ms; after chooser:v2.4 p50=42ms p99=290ms. avg writev ops/request +22%. KV hit-rate steady.

priya: So not a kvcache coldstart. Looks like framing fragmentation is the driver. We should either revert the chooser or reduce fragmentation by increasing coalesce window in the pool config.

sasha: I prototyped a small change: when chooser picks scalar fast-path emit a kvcache-prefetch hint for the request (prefetch keys observed in header proto). That reduced observed writev ops -8% in microbench.

ash: Nice. Another angle: batcher coalesce param. For pool-7, coalesce_window default=32. If we increase to 48 we saw fewer microframes in a local sim. Might be less ideal for latency-sensitive single-frame requests though.

morgan: Let's not apply two changes at once. Step 1 revert on canary, collect pprof + writev counter. Step 2 run controlled A/B: chooser=scalar vs chooser=hybrid (scalar only when frag_count==0 and seq_len>20) and a second dimension with kvcache-prefetch on/off.

deploy-bot: pool-7 rollback initiated by morgan at 2026-03-23T18:10:01Z  status: in_progress.

priya: I'll add a lightweight counter to the inet stack: request.metrics.writev_count and expose it to /metrics/request for correlation.

sasha: Repro command I used locally:
```bash
./tools/replay --trace traces/ingress/2026-03-22.ndjson --chooser scalar --samples 2000 --pprof out/pprof.scalar
./tools/replay --trace traces/ingress/2026-03-22.ndjson --chooser hybrid --samples 2000 --pprof out/pprof.hybrid
```
Bench: scalar p50 host CPU +8% vs hybrid. Hybrid kept vectorized utf8 in most fragmenting cases.

ash: We'll need a unit test for chooser that synthesizes fragmented http2 keepalive burst shapes. I can add a fuzz harness to generate fragments count distribution.

morgan: Good. Also collect strace on a canary host for a short window to count write syscalls vs writev. That will confirm syscall overhead.

deploy-bot: rollback completed at 2026-03-23T18:13:22Z  pool-7 reverted to kernel-chooser:v2.3.

replay-bot: running A/B now with tags: chooser:scalar, chooser:hybrid and kvcache-prefetch:on/off. Will push aggregated CSV to s3 when done.

priya: I pushed the writev_count metric and a dashboard panel (ingress -> host -> writev_count per request). Link: https://dash.redwood/boards/ingress-writev.

sasha: If A/B confirms hybrid keeps CPU down and prefetch reduces writev ops further, we can ship hybrid + prefetch. If hybrid alone suffices, skip prefetch to reduce complexity.

morgan: Agreed. Timeline: A/B finishes in ~90m, PR for hybrid + unit tests from ash tomorrow, and we'll run 6h validation on canary before prod rollout.

ash: Opening PR: "chooser: hybrid gating + fragmentation fuzz tests". Will include perf numbers and bench scripts.

morgan: Thanks everyone  closing thread until the 6h results land."
